$about: DOC-12 round, 2026-08-06: the landing page defect (four places stating 1.0.12 beside one stating 1.0.13) fixed at the page and, more importantly, at the two guards that reported green while it shipped. Run against this project's own repository - self-assessment, not third-party evidence; the target row says so, and is depth L1 so it can never be read as an adoption. Every quotation below is literal output from a command run in the working tree at the commit this observation lands with.

observations.evidence: Reproduced first: `grep -o '[0-9]*\.[0-9]*\.[0-9]*' site/index.html | sort | uniq -c` returned `4 1.0.12` and `1 1.0.13` (plus 15 coordinate triples from SVG path data), against `VERSION` = 1.0.13 - the header pill correct, the maturity disclosure (line 973), the footer (line 983) and two hero-script lines (1010, 1018) a release behind. Both guards were green on that exact tree: `node tools/site-check.mjs` printed `ok    site/index.html: advertises v1.0.13 (matches VERSION)` and exited `site-check: OK - landing + docsite shippable`, and `node standard/scripts/facts-check.mjs` printed `ok    standard-version = 1.0.13 - 5 restatement(s) agree`, because its only declared pattern for this file (`class="tag mono">v`) points at the one occurrence that was right. Fixed: the four strings now read 1.0.13, and site-check compares every version-shaped string on the landing against VERSION rather than asserting one of them appears - `ok    site/index.html: all 5 version string(s) on the page state 1.0.13`. Verified the new check actually fires by putting the footer back to v1.0.12 on the real landing: `FAIL  site/index.html:983: states 1.0.12, and VERSION says 1.0.13 ("...<span>repository-standards · v1.0.12 · MIT<...")`, `site-check: FAIL - 1 problem(s)` - while facts-check on that same tree still printed `ok    standard-version = 1.0.13 - 5 restatement(s) agree`, confirming the gap was site-check's to close. Exactly one problem was reported, not eighteen, because `<svg>` bodies are masked before the scan: the landing's own marks carry 17 version-shaped coordinate triples (6.1.8, 3.3.7, 1.2.1, 1.1.8 and so on), and a check that failed on those would have been switched off within a day. `tools/site-check-test.mjs` is new and holds the behaviour: 5 cases over fixture sites, `site-check-test: OK - 5 cases, a landing carrying a second version cannot pass`, including a fixture whose path data is literally `d="M1.9.9 4.5.6 2.3.9"` next to a correct version, and a stale-footer case asserting the run reports `FAIL - 1 problem(s)` so the mask cannot silently stop working. No new facts.json patterns: the remaining four occurrences are prose, footer layout and hero copy, and facts-check fails when a declared pattern stops matching, so enumerating them would block the next rewording and still miss whatever is added after - the scan needs no list. Recorded as a caveat rather than hidden: this fixes the landing this repository publishes, and no mechanism yet stops a stale version on an ecosystem sibling's landing that carries its own VERSION.
